items.title: Man Utd will reject any bid for Fernandes
items.description: Manchester United have no intention of selling captain Bruno Fernandes despite Turkish club Galatasaray being prepared to lodge a bid for the 31-year-old later this week.

items.title: Man City move for £85m Bouaddi and still want Fernandez
items.description: Manchester City are in advanced talks with Lille over a move for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

items.title: No Draper as Fery named in GB's Davis Cup squad
items.description: Arthur Fery has been named in the Great Britain Davis Cup team for the home qualifying tie against Ecuador next month.

items.title: MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year joins Hundred final coverage
items.description: The MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year for 2026, Rosa Simkin, received the ultimate competition prize when joining Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday.

items.title: From Chelsea bomb squad to new chapter at Como for Chalobah
items.description: After ending his near 20-year association with Chelsea by joining Como 1907 this summer, Trevoh Chalobah credits his time at Stamford Bridge with building his resilience.

items.title: £2.14bn and counting - why Premier League spending could set new record
items.description: Premier League clubs have spent £2.14bn this summer, with huge sums moving between top-flight rivals. BBC Sport examines the possibility of a new spending record.

items.title: Pocognoli 'feels connection' with 'passionate' Scotland
items.description: New Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli says the passionate nature of Scottish football was a key factor in his taking the job.

items.title: Maresca's Man City problems are more than a missing midfield
items.description: Enzo Maresca spoke of his desire to "close the gap" between Manchester City and Arsenal before watching his side suffer a painful 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield on Sunday. Perhaps the gaping holes through the spine of his team should be more of an immediate area of focus.

items.title: Scottish FA withdraws support for Fifa president Infantino
items.description: The Scottish Football Association has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino and will not be voting for his re-election as president of Fifa, chief executive Ian Maxwell has told BBC Sport.
